{"full_source_conversation":"seeker: Hey, are you around? I could really use someone to talk to.
supporter: Of course, Emily. I'm here for you. What's going on?
seeker: Bob and I had a big argument last night. I haven't been able to stop thinking about it.
supporter: I'm sorry to hear that. Arguments can be really tough. Do you want to share what happened?
seeker: Yeah, it just spiraled out of control. We started talking about our finances, and it just got heated.
supporter: Financial pressures can put so much strain on relationships. It's completely understandable to feel overwhelmed. How are you feeling now?
seeker: Exhausted, honestly. It's like we're stuck in this cycle of stress, and I don't see a way out.
supporter: It sounds really challenging, Emily. It's okay to feel this way. Have you two been able to talk it out since it happened?
seeker: Not yet. We both needed some space. Bob went for a drive, and I've just been trying to calm down.
supporter: Taking some space can be helpful to gather thoughts. Do you think you’ll be ready to talk soon?
seeker: I hope so. I don't want to keep ignoring it, but I'm also scared it'll turn into another argument.
supporter: That's understandable. Talking during a calm moment might help. Maybe planning a time to chat could prevent it from escalating?
seeker: That's a good idea. Maybe after dinner tonight. I just wish he would understand how stressed I am too.
supporter: Your feelings are very valid, Emily. It's important for both of you to feel heard. Do you feel like you can express how you’re both feeling?
seeker: I want to, but sometimes I don’t know how to start without sounding like I’m blaming him.
supporter: Starting with 'I feel' statements can help focus on your emotions rather than assigning blame. It's okay to express vulnerability.
seeker: That's true. I'll try that. Thanks for reminding me. I just want us to be okay.
supporter: You’re doing your best, and that is important. Figuring it out together might bring you closer. How are you taking care of yourself today?
seeker: I haven’t really done much for myself yet. Maybe I should go for a walk or listen to some music.
supporter: That sounds like a wonderful idea. Taking a little time for self-care can help clear your mind and give you strength.
seeker: Thanks for listening. It really helps just having someone to talk to about all this.
supporter: I'm always here for you, Emily. Take it one step at a time, and keep me updated if you need anything.
seeker: I will. Thanks again.","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2024-10-10","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

{"full_source_conversation":"supporter: Hello
seeker: Hello, I hope you can help me.
supporter: Sure I can
seeker: I work hard at my job in an office.  We acquired another company and my job is now twice the work.
seeker: Two of my coworkers have gotten a raise and I have not gotten anything!
supporter: Have you talked to your boss about it?
seeker: I have hinted around that my job is sooo busy and he knows it, I haven't come out and said anything yet.
supporter: I can understand how you feeling you work extremely hard and get no raise when you deserve it
seeker: Yes, I have been at the job for 15 years and make a decent salary but this amount of work is insane.  Do you think I should bring it up to him>
supporter: oh wow 15 years? I really believe you need a raise and doing more work now.
supporter: I honestly think you should bring it up to your boss
seeker: Yes, I think so too.  I like my boss but he is funny about things sometimes.  Any ideas on how I could bring it up to him.  I hate feeling this way, my attitude is really turning sour.
supporter: I can't believe he has not given you a raise by now 
seeker: I know!
supporter: Just tell him that you need to have a serious talk with him and tell him straight up what is on your mind don't hold it back
seeker: So, I guess I'll have to be honest and brave at the same time.  
seeker: Do you think I should bring in proof....paperwork, etc.  I have been working extra as well.
supporter: Yes I know you can do it but that is the only way to solve the situation is by communicating with him
supporter: Yes that would help more by bringing in proof to him 
seeker: Ok, I am just so angry over the whole thing, I'm going to have to keep my cool and let him know without getting an attitude, do you think that will work?
supporter: Yes just remain calm with him 
seeker: I will try, I hope I don't start crying!  I tend to get frustrated and cry.
supporter: getting a attitude with him will not help at all 
seeker: Yes, you are right, it will make it a bad situation.
supporter: Don't let this situation get to you so much 
seeker: O
seeker: oops
seeker: I'll try not to, I have to be calm, like you said
supporter: Everything will be ok
seeker: Thank you so much for your positive support!
seeker: I'll let him know I need to talk and I'll remain calm
supporter: Your welcome i am sure he will give you a raise once you talk to him
seeker: Fingers crossed!  I really have gone above and beyond and feel I really deserve it.
supporter: I will be praying that you get the raise because you deserve it
seeker: Thank you so much, you've been very helpful!
supporter: Your most welcome
seeker: Merry Christmas!
supporter: Merry Christmas to you to!","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2024-07-01","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

{"full_source_conversation":"seeker: Hi I am seeking support to assist me with better sleep patterns.
supporter: Hi there, let me get a deeper understanding of your existing sleep pattern. Do you suffer from insomnia or another type of sleep disorder? 
seeker: No, it is not insomnia.  
supporter: Okay, are you drinking enough water and eating a healthy diet? 
seeker: I could improve my water intake and eat more vegatables.
supporter: I like to analyze my own habits every now and then, it helps me stay in check. You can definitely benefit from meditating and self reflecting. 
seeker: Thanks!  What other ideas do you have?
supporter: Of course! I always knock right out after a workout. But if you aren't able to, just simple things like turning all the lights off at the same time every night and laying in bed will help. It will align your circadian rhythm! 
seeker: Great, but I wake up frequently thinking about the recent events surrounding police and how they treat black people.
supporter: It definitely is a valid reason to be kept awake. The only good part about something so horrible, is that you have the power to make sure you will continue to be a good person. If everyone was as empathetic as you, the world would be a better place. Thank you for caring so deeply about such a brutal matter. 
seeker: I wish there were more caring people in the world. 
supporter: Kindness is contagious, and you definitely have a kind heart. As long as you remain soft in a hard world, people will recognize that and follow suit. The world is becoming more aware, and we have the power to raise future generations with more knowledge and love for one another. Caring doesn't come naturally to many unfortunately, but the ways of inspiring the people that don't care, are endless. We as a society can definitely think of more ways to care for one another. 
seeker: Correct, but having a kind heart does not keep me from waking up & worrying about my son and other black men in my family. 
supporter: I worry about my sons and husband and father all the time... I shift my focus on loving them and cherishing every moment we have together. Police or not, the time we have is not promised.. 
seeker: That's good advice.
seeker: Are you still there?
supporter: A hot cup of tea never hurt too! But in all seriousness, I can completely understand your sleep troubles. It is much deeper than just that. Perspective is the key to life. You are a strong and empathetic soul. 
seeker: okay
seeker: Love conquers all
supporter: That is so beautifully true 
seeker: I'm looking forward to a fulls night rest. 
supporter: That is good, lavender baths or showers will also ease and relax the troubled mind. 
seeker: Relaxing is good therapy. 
supporter: I like to relax with a book and a blanket sometimes too. 
seeker: Self care is needed.
supporter: Self care is definitely something we can overlook accidentally. Being self aware is a daily practice.
seeker: I agree.  Loving ourselves & the ones we care about too.  
supporter: It is good that we spoke today, I am going to hug my sons a little harder when I see them tonight. ","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2024-09-06","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

{"full_source_conversation":"seeker: Hey, I needed someone to talk to about everything that's been going on.
supporter: Of course, Emily. I'm here for you. How have things been since you started therapy?
seeker: It's been a bit overwhelming, to be honest. I'm glad I took the step, but it's a lot to unpack.
supporter: It sounds like you're processing a lot. It's completely normal to feel overwhelmed. What's been on your mind?
seeker: Mainly my relationship with Bob and the financial strain. It's hard not to feel angry and resentful sometimes.
supporter: That's understandable. Financial pressures can really strain relationships. How are you both handling it right now?
seeker: We're trying to talk more without arguing, but it's a struggle. I can't help but feel frustrated thinking about how he left his job.
supporter: I can hear the frustration and it's valid. It must be tough carrying the burden alone. How is the therapy helping you with these feelings?
seeker: Therapy helps, slowly. It's nice to have a space to express myself, but it doesn't change things immediately at home.
supporter: Having an outlet is important. Therapy can sometimes take time, but it's great you're making progress. Are there things you're learning that help?
seeker: I learned about setting boundaries and communicating my needs. It’s something I’m working on with Bob.
supporter: That sounds like a positive step. How is Bob responding to the changes you're trying to make?
seeker: I think he's trying, but it's hard to change old habits, especially when both of us are stressed.
supporter: Change is challenging, especially during tough times. Acknowledging the effort on both sides is a good step. What about your job? How's that affecting things?
seeker: Work is another stress. They doubled my workload after an acquisition, but no raise came with it.
supporter: That sounds incredibly unfair and stressful. No wonder you feel overwhelmed with everything piling up.
seeker: It is. I'm trying to manage my mental health, but sometimes it feels like too much.
supporter: It's okay to feel that way. It seems like you're doing your best despite everything. Are you able to find any small ways to de-stress?
seeker: I try to take walks and focus on mindfulness exercises. They help me feel a little more grounded.
supporter: That's great to hear. It's important to celebrate these small wins. seeker: Hello, I am looking for help in managing some depression.
supporter: You've come to a good place to start.
supporter: Is there something in particular that is leaving you feeling depressed?
seeker: I am feeling resentful towards my husband for quitting his job, and my son for being the reason that he quit his job.
seeker: My son's behavior is causing a lot of conflict in our house and my husband not working is putting a lot of financial stress on us
supporter: I'm sorry to hear that. Feeling resentment for both your husband's loss of work and your son's loss of his job is entirely understandable. 
seeker: I have a hard time not dwelling on the negative things going on.  It's hard to see anything positive or feel hopeful for the future.

seeker: Thank you. I've been trying to figure out how to handle this. The financial strain with Bob, and now Jerry acting out... it's just a lot.
supporter: That does sound overwhelming. How have you been managing everything?
seeker: Therapy helps, but outside of that, I just try to keep my head above water.
supporter: I'm glad you've found some support in therapy. What strategies have been helping you there?
seeker: The therapist has been teaching me breathing techniques and we've been working on expressing my feelings more constructively.
supporter: That sounds really valuable. Do you think any of those techniques could help with how you're feeling about Jerry?
seeker: Perhaps. I think I need to communicate better with him and find out what's really going on beneath the surface.
supporter: It sounds like you have a great approach. Being able to talk openly with him might really help both of you.
seeker: I hope so. I just want to make sure he understands that I care about him, even when I’m upset.

seeker: It was tense. The principal was understanding but firm. I just felt so disappointed and a bit like I've failed him.
